rationale: This benchmark is a set of tiny (64-200 byte text), extremely hot numeric kernels (fannkuch, n-body, spectral-norm inner loops) plus a recursion-heavy group (tak, takFP, fib, fibFP, puzzle), so overhead-sensitive passes must be restrained while cheap, always-safe diversity is favored. SUB gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights and minimal cost weights because instruction substitution is essentially free at runtime and size, making it the dominant source of resistance here. BCF and FLA receive elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights so the selector avoids applying them inside the hot inner loops and recursive call chains where their dispatcher and clone overhead would dominate; FLA additionally gets a low benefit weight since these functions are too small for flattening to add meaningful structural confusion. IBR is similarly gated with a high RuntimeCost weight because indirect branching on the tak/fib recursion and hot loops is costly, while ICALL is down-weighted on both benefit and cost since these kernels make almost no indirect calls to hide. SPLIT is effectively suppressed (high SizeCost, low benefit) because the functions are already tiny and splitting would only bloat the 721-byte text footprint; IGV is kept at moderate values as a middle-ground option for the array/global accesses in nsieve-bits and n-body without meaningfully impacting the hot loops.
